summary: Module 5 REFLECT. ITERATION EFFICIENCY: total iterations across the team feature = 3 refinements (M2 Task2 restart+repair counted as 1 restart + 1 refinement, M3 redact 1 refinement, M4 IDOR 0 refinements -- guard in prompt from round 1); used well under the 4-budget per task. Restarts: 1 (M2 Task 1 -> Task 2), and hindsight says YES it was right -- the schema contract conflict was structural and a targeted patch would have built on the wrong foundation. Quality trajectory: monotonic up (R1 structural restart -> R2-R4 structural 4,4,5 / surface 3,4,5); no plateau, no regression. Final quality: Structural 5/5, Surface 5/5 -- ships. DECISION QUALITY: every refine-vs-restart call was right; the spiral in Step 5 I recognized via the trajectory data (the verify proof had already pinned structural+surface rising), and my contract-check made the detection concrete rather than vibes. Confidence in surface-vs-structural: high, and it matched accuracy -- the M2 call (structural) and M3 call (surface, single edit fixed it) both validated by outcomes. STRATEGY ASSESSMENT: two-iteration rule served perfectly; refine-first would have wasted 2+ iterations on the M2 schema conflict, restart-early would have needlessly discarded the M3 redact fix and M4 first-pass guards. Personal restart threshold: structural quality below ~3/5 with surface below ~3/5 on round 2 -> restart; any regression on an earlier achievement -> restart immediately. PROMPT EVOLUTION: first prompt (M2 Task 1) was feature-level; last prompts embed the interface contract verbatim + failure-mode constraints (never prompt from plan assumptions; embed upstream actual output). The failed iterations taught me the 'plan-vs-output divergence' failure mode -- unknowable without trying. From scratch now: my first prompt would include the interface-contract discipline from prompt #1. BROADER PATTERN: the skills apply to state machines, multi-step transactions, concurrent access, security-critical flows -- my IDOR work in M4 was exactly a security-critical case where the guard-in-prompt (constraint) approach prevented iterations entirely.
